slot_note: wave 3, new; numbered from seed FC16 (express-carrier customs brokerage), world, decision and quantity only
niche: an express carrier's annual broker establishment review in Canada: where six funded customs broker posts go across five import gateway brokerage desks for 2027, or are held, on each desk's forecast 2027 formal entries per broker post, when a shipment needs a broker's formal entry only above CAD 3,300 once its invoice value is converted at the customs rate, the network plan sets 2027's exchange rates, and the goods differ in whether their prices are set in the invoice currency or in Canadian dollars
answer: Place two of the six new broker posts at Dorval and one at Calgary for 2027, and hold the other three to the next review.
stakeholder_role: the brokerage workforce planning lead in the carrier's Canadian customs brokerage department, who prepares the annual broker establishment review

spine.file: highvalue_check_2024Q4.csv to highvalue_check_2026Q3.csv (eight quarterly extracts: the four of the plan's base and the four pulled for the 2026 review)
spine.entity: one inbound international shipment released at a gateway with a value for duty of CAD 2,500 or more, or under an OGD program, with its importer, tariff item, declared value in its invoice currency, the customs rate of its date and the route the clearance system gave it, over the two years to September 2026
spine.source: constructed (the clearance system's quarterly high-value check extracts, two layouts)

world.geography: Canada (five import gateways at Mississauga, Dorval, Richmond, Calgary and Winnipeg; the express carrier, its contract broker, people, systems and data are fictional)
world.org_type: an express carrier's Canadian customs brokerage department and its five gateway brokerage desks

driver: The forward count of units above a fixed line is set by where each unit's value lands at the forward period's conversion factors, and units differ in which value they hold fixed from period to period, their own denomination or the line's; the history's count carries only the past factors, a mechanical re-conversion of every unit treats every unit as holding its own denomination, and one pooled share of holders treats unlike groups alike, so only estimating each group's mix of holders from the units seen in both periods, and re-converting the own-denomination share alone, gets the count.
driver_concrete: Each gateway's 2027 formal entries are its shipments of the twelve months to September 2026 routed for the plan year with each segment's exchange-rate pass-through: by gateway and invoice currency, the share of the base year's repeat consignments that kept their invoice value (and so carry the rate into their CAD value) against those that kept their CAD value; that share is re-routed at the network plan's 2027 planning rate against the CAD 3,300 line, the rest keeps the route the base year gave it, OGD-regulated shipments formal whatever their value, scaled to the plan's volumes. Calgary's US-dollar goods (0.009) and the Chinese goods at Mississauga and Richmond (0.011, 0.013) hold their CAD values while every other segment keeps its invoice prices (0.958 to 1.000), so Dorval gains about an eighth at the plan's euro rate of 1.68, Mississauga, Richmond and Winnipeg lose about a tenth at the plan's US dollar rate of 1.34, and Calgary stays where it was.
stump: Carrying each gateway's formal entries per inbound shipment of the twelve months to September 2026 onto the 2027 network plan places one post at each of the five gateways and holds one; the step that lands it there is forecasting the 2027 count without estimating how each segment's CAD values respond to the plan's exchange rates, and re-routing every shipment at those rates instead (or one pooled pass-through share) drops Calgary's post and holds four.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the staffing standard, the clearance manual and the network plan correctly forecasts each gateway's 2027 formal entries as the plan's shipments times its formal entries per shipment over the twelve months to September 2026 and places one post at each of the five gateways with one held. The stronger one who sees that the plan's rates move the line re-routes every base-year shipment at its own currency's planning rate, because the clearance manual values a shipment on its invoice, and files two posts at Dorval with four held (Calgary at 2,000 a month); one pass-through share for the network (0.737) or for each currency (0.719 for the US dollar) files the same. Only estimating the pass-through by gateway and invoice currency from the consignments repeated across the two years (Calgary's US-dollar goods and the Chinese goods at Mississauga and Richmond keep their CAD values, every other segment its invoice prices) and re-routing the invoice-held share alone files two at Dorval, one at Calgary and three held.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each gateway's 2027 formal entries, which trade economics forecasts conditionally on the plan year's exchange rates as the mass of declared values above a line fixed in Canadian dollars, the rate reaching each value only as far as its goods are priced in the invoice currency (producer-currency against local-currency pricing, the pass-through the field estimates from repeat transactions); with another field's nouns (a hospital's admissions, a utility's megawatt-hours) there is no invoice currency, no pricing currency to choose and no nominal line for a converted value to cross, so the forecast that decides the call has nothing to stand on.
layer1: the clearance system's high-value check extracts in eight quarterly files, the layout changed by a February 2026 release (column names, date formats, the rate column's label)
release times stamped in UTC beside each gateway's local release date
the monthly gateway report in two layouts: the legacy brokerage system to September 2024 counting formal entries by accounting date, the new system from October 2024 by release date
gateways keyed by airport code in one file, by desk name in another and by region label in the network plan
the network plan's volumes in thousands of shipments to one decimal
shipments invoiced in Canadian dollars beside US dollars, euros, sterling, renminbi and yen, each row with the customs rate of its date
other-government-department program codes on the register, blank or NONE where none applies
shipments amended after release appearing again in the next quarter's extract with the corrected value

time and attendance in two systems (legacy to 31 October 2025, new from 1 November 2025), employee numbers and pay codes in two schemes, the migration carrying the last open week of October into the new system
HR assignment history in effective-dated rows for brokers who moved between desks
call-back lines carrying the paid minimum beside the punch times

the contract broker's monthly invoices dated in the month after the entries they bill, its portal detail repeating each invoice's desk-minimum adjustment on every line, and a disputed invoice re-issued with its credit memo posted after the year end

differentiation.task127: task127 v3 restates a development triangle's history at the latest resolution shares before carrying its age-to-age ratios; here nothing develops by age: a fixed nominal line is re-applied to each shipment's own invoice-currency value at the plan year's exchange rates, a conversion the history never ran at.
differentiation.task138: task138 rebuilds each unit's starting store from its replenishment record before replaying past driver traces; here no state carries forward and nothing is replayed: the plan year's exchange rates move a fixed Canadian-dollar line across each shipment's invoice value.
differentiation.task446: task446 backs a moved base rate out through a screen's two error rates (Bayes' rule on a classifier); here there is no classifier and no base rate: the count above a nominal line is the upper tail of declared values under the plan year's exchange rates, and the decisive estimate is which goods carry the rate into their CAD value, read segment by segment off repeat consignments.

notes: stump_strategy forecast_method_backtest (stumping strategies F6): the quantity the history shows (formal entries, their share of shipments, a fitted elasticity) is not the invariant, and neither is every shipment's invoice value: the invariant is each consignment's price in the currency it is set in, and the segments differ, so the natural fits fail forward. No back-test organ ships: the method is forced by the design (the routing rule converts each value at the rate of its date, the plan sets 2027's rates, the repeat consignments of the two years on file show each segment's pass-through). Gap time decisive (the plan year's rates against the history's), population second (the segments' pricing currencies differ; OGD-regulated shipments are formal whatever their value). Furniture: forum executive_team (the Canada leadership team approves the establishment on 22 October 2026), forcing event vote_or_meeting (that establishment review), organisation family logistics_or_3pl (an express carrier). Stage 4 repair (2026-10-15): the plan's profile no longer files invoice prices and the plan's growth was re-set so entries per post round alike from the unrounded and the rounded forecast. Rule 3 rework (2026-10-15): the full re-pricing at the plan's rates read as a filed assumption executed through a filed rule, so the decisive step moved to the exchange-rate pass-through estimated by gateway and invoice currency from the repeat consignments; the call is kept.
